title: All-American Apple Pie
kicker: A lattice that took patience, apples that kept their spine, and a filling that never turns to soup.
story: Apple pie's reputation as American shorthand hides a much older passport — English apple pyes date to the 14th century, often with savory intents. The American move was the double crust, the lattice, and the confidence that dessert can be the main event. Done right, it is an engineering project: a bottom crust that stays crisp under a lake of fruit, a filling thick enough to slice, a top that shatters.

The three secrets are apple selection, pre-cooking, and flour discipline. Use a mix of apples — tart Granny Smiths for structure, a sweet variety for flavor. Pre-cook the filling briefly so the apples collapse first in the pan instead of inside the pie, which creates the dreaded gap under the lid. And thicken with just enough flour or cornstarch; the juices should turn to jam, not wallpaper paste.
fun_fact: 'As American as apple pie' — but the apple itself is an immigrant, and during WWII soldiers answered 'mom and apple pie' when asked what they fought for. The phrase outlived the war.

ingredients.note: 2.5 cups flour, 220 g cold butter, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp sugar, ice water — chilled 1 hr minimum
half Granny Smith, half Golden Delicious or Honeycrisp

steps.title: Dough first, always ahead
steps.text: Make the dough by cutting cold butter into flour until pea-sized rubble remains, add ice water until it just holds, divide in two, flatten, wrap, chill an hour. Cold butter chunks = flaky layers. Warm butter = cardboard.

steps.title: Pre-cook the filling
steps.text: Peel, core, slice apples 1 cm thick. Toss with sugars, flour, spices, lemon, salt. Cook in a wide pan over medium 8-10 minutes until juices thicken and apples just bend. Cool completely — this is the anti-gap, anti-sog move.

steps.title: Roll the bottom
steps.text: Roll the first disc 3 mm thick, a circle larger than the pan. Drape into a 23 cm / 9-inch dish, press into the corner without stretching (stretched dough shrinks), leave the overhang.

steps.title: Fill high and proud
steps.text: Pile the cooled filling in the center — it sinks as it bakes, so mound it. Dot with butter. Brush the rim with egg so the lid welds on.

steps.title: Lattice (or a vented lid)
steps.text: Roll the second disc, cut 2.5 cm strips, weave over the filling — over, under, repeat — or lay a full lid with 5 vents cut. Trim, fold, crimp the edge. Egg wash and coarse sugar everywhere.

steps.title: Bake the two-stage bake
steps.text: 220°C / 425°F for 20 minutes to set the lid, then 180°C / 350°F for 40-45 minutes until the filling bubbles through the vents — bubbling means the thickener worked. Foil-shield the rim if it darkens fast. Cool 3 hours minimum. Slicing hot pie is filling assassination.

notes: The 3-hour cool is real: the filling sets as it cools, and warm pie slices into soup. Warm-ish after 3 hours is the perfect state.
Dough scraps rerolled with cinnamon sugar make baker's snacks — the cook's tax.
Serve with sharp cheddar slices (New England style) or vanilla ice cream. Choose a side in the war, or eat both.

storage: Room temperature 2 days under a dome, refrigerate after — re-crisp slices in a 180°C / 350°F oven for 10 minutes. Baked pie freezes 3 months; thaw and re-crisp.

the lemon keeps the apples from browning
egg wash for the lacquered top

facts.first_recorded: 1381 — a printed recipe in The Forme of Cury
facts.name_means: Exactly what it says. The honesty is the point.
facts.technique: Blind bake the bottom, thicken the filling, vent the roof
facts.signature: Cinnamon, butter pastry, apples holding their shape
facts.serve_at: Warm, with cold cream running into the gap
facts.pour: Hot coffee, or cold cider if you have it
